definitions.explanation: knowledge and shrewdness gained through experience in social dealings and worldly affairs

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{世故|せこ}に{長|た}けている。
examples.english: He is well versed in the ways of the world.

examples.japanese: {世故|せこ}に{通|つう}じた{人|ひと}は{交渉|こうしょう}がうまい。
examples.english: People who are worldly-wise are good at negotiations.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いのに{世故|せこ}に{長|た}けた{彼女|かのじょ}の{立|た}ち{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いに、{周囲|しゅうい}の{大人|おとな}たちは{感心|かんしん}した。
examples.english: The adults around her were impressed by her worldly-wise conduct despite her young age.

notes:
A literary term for the practical wisdom one gains through social experience and navigating worldly affairs. Often appears in the set phrase {世故|せこ}に{長|た}ける (to be experienced in worldly matters). Can carry a slightly negative nuance, suggesting someone is too calculating or shrewd.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {世故|せこ}に{長|た}ける: to be worldly-wise, to be socially experienced
- {世故|せこ}に{通|つう}じる: to be well versed in the ways of the world
- {世故|せこ}に{疎|うと}い: to be naive about worldly affairs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {世渡|よわた}り: getting along in the world — more practical, everyday term for navigating life
- {処世|しょせい}: conduct in life — formal term for how one handles life's affairs
- {老獪|ろうかい}: cunning/wily — implies shrewd experience with a negative connotation
